observations:
Torah #185 is a compact, unified teaching with a single conceptual domain: the two types of yir'ah (fear/awe of God) and the structural decomposition of the upper yir'ah into the letter alef (yud + vav + dalet). All bechina concepts — whether already in the dataset or identified as gaps — belong to this single domain and are adequately captured by Package 1 (יִרְאָה וְאוֹת אָלֶ"ף).

No independent domain of 3+ concepts was found that is structurally separate from the existing package:

1. The lower yir'ah concepts (יראה תחתונה, אד, העלאת מיין נוקבין) are NOT a separate package — they are the lesser grade of the same yir'ah domain. The Torah explicitly presents both types of yir'ah as aspects of a single phenomenon (both relate to dalet/malkhut: the upper is a fully formed dalet, the lower is 'dalei dalet' — a double-poor dalet), and distinguishes them only in their source and their effect, not in their essential nature.

2. The vessel concepts (כלי, מם סתומה, אדם) arise directly from the lower yir'ah's function and are not an independent domain — the vessel is what is needed once the lower yir'ah draws down shefa. These three concepts together could theoretically form a small cluster, but they are entirely subordinate to and dependent on the yir'ah teaching. They do not constitute a standalone thematic domain.

3. The ציון / צייר ורושם הכלי concept (from the appended section) is itself an extension of the vessel concept, and thus doubly subordinate to the yir'ah package.

The good/evil mirror structure: Torah #185 has no evil package. This is consistent with the Torah's nature — it is a positive, instructional teaching about the two grades of yir'ah, their mechanisms, and their respective effects on divine completeness and worldly abundance. The lower yir'ah (coming from lower fears) is not evil — it is a legitimate, if lesser, path to yir'ah. The Torah does not describe an opposing evil domain; there is no anti-yir'ah or anti-malkhut discussed as an evil counterpart in this teaching.

Conclusion: The single Package 1 fully encompasses all concepts in Torah #185. With the gap additions identified in torah_185_additions.json incorporated, the package would grow to approximately 10–11 nodes, all sharing the single theme of yir'ah / alef / malkhut. No new package is warranted.
